Run a SAS program on the R engine

Source: R/run.R
sas_run.Rd

The macro processor hands complete steps to the executor one at a time (at RUN; / QUIT; / step boundaries), so CALL SYMPUT(X) results are visible to the macro code that follows the step, including inside macro bodies.

Usage

sas_run(
  code,
  work = list(),
  level = c("auto", "L3"),
  on_error = getOption("sasonr.on_error", c("sas", "abort")),
  session = NULL
)

Arguments

code

SAS source code.

work

Named list of input data frames available as WORK data sets.

level

"auto" (choose L1/L2/L3 per step) or "L3" (force row loops).

on_error

What an ERROR of the program does (a syntax error, an unknown function, a missing input data set, an ERROR in PROC SQL ...). "sas" (the default; option sasonr.on_error) uses the batch-mode error handling: the failing step is not run, syntax-check mode (OBS=0) applies to the rest of the program (later steps are compiled but not run; global statements and the macro language still are), SYSERR/SYSCC are set and the result has status = "error", the ERROR lines in $log and WORK as the failing step leaves it. "abort" stops with the classed R condition instead. Features sasonr does not support (sasonr_unsupported) always stop the run: they are not errors of the program.

session

A session from sas_session(): the program runs as one more submission to it (WORK, macro variables, user formats, options and titles of earlier submissions are visible; work data sets are added to its WORK). NULL (the default) runs in a fresh session that is discarded afterwards.

Value

A sasonr_result: $log (the log: the program lines with the NOTEs, WARNINGs, ERRORs and PUT output; see sas_log()), $log_events (a tibble of the log events), $listing (procedure output), $ods (the ODS tables of the procedure output in output order, each a sas_ods_table; PROC MEANS and SUMMARY), $work (output data sets with trailing blanks removed), $translation, $macro_vars (global macro variables), $status ("ok" or "error"), $errors (the ERROR messages) and $error_line (SAS line of the first ERROR). With a session, $log, $log_events, $listing, $translation, $status and $errors describe this submission, $work and $macro_vars the whole session.

Examples

res <- sas_run("
data class;
  input name $ age;
  length group $ 5;
  if age >= 13 then group = 'teen'; else group = 'child';
  datalines;
Alice 12
Bob 14
;
run;
proc print data=class; run;
")
res$work$class
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   name    age group
#>   <chr> <dbl> <chr>
#> 1 Alice    12 child
#> 2 Bob      14 teen 
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#> Obs    name     age    group
#> 
#>   1    Alice     12    child
#>   2    Bob       14    teen
